create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), 1<<L<<H<=J^(1/2), R_0=ceil(L), and M=M_L asymp L^2. Retain the complete literal residual near-square opening c_N^rem=sum_(d|N,d odd)chi_4(d)lambda_N(d), with D_L<<_epsilon L^2X^epsilon, d,m asymp L, bounded opened weights and divisor multiplicity, every selected/no-pair value, squarefree/coprimality mask, two-adic branch, profile, endpoint, point value, and zero extension. For every stopped-chain link R<T<=2R, open an ordered even-gap atom by d'=d+2s, m'=m+v, v even, and r_s=dv+2s(m+v), on the complete d>0 odd, m>=1, s in Z literal domain. Then chi_4(d')chi_4(d)=(-1)^s and the exact link is Delta_(R,T)=2Re sum (-1)^s beta_(R,T)(r_s)G(s). The bandpass is globally 1/T-Lipschitz, r_(s+1)-r_s=2m' asymp L on nonzero literal support, and the complete opened incidence ledger proves sum_j|C_(R_j,R_(j+1))|<<_epsilon L^3X^epsilon for C_(R,T)=Re sum (-1)^s(beta(r_s)-beta(r_(s+1)))G(s), including every cusp and the strict final link. The finite alternating identity gives Delta=C+R with R_(R,T)=Re sum (-1)^s beta(r_(s+1))(G(s)-G(s+1)). Exact full-line reindexing gives R_(R,T)=Re sum (-1)^s(beta(r_s)+beta(r_(s+1)))G(s)=Delta_(R,T)-C_(R,T). Hence on the complete stopped chain sum_j R_j=2(T_26+B_short)-sum_j C_j, with B_short<<_epsilon L^3X^epsilon, so the one-sided remainder target is equivalent to K26 modulo target-safe terms. Coefficient-uniform positive or absolute closure of the adjacent-sum remainder has available upper scale RL^2X^epsilon, reaching L^4X^epsilon at a maximal link; phase-adapted sharpness is nonliteral and is not physical lower mass. On all-1 mod 4 no-pair support, active tangent sites are even and the two birth/death differences add, an allowed-support warning but not a density theorem or owner-complete sector. The no-go covers only this displayed tangent first-difference, its adjoint or tautological second-Abel transfer, and positivity before an actual-symbol gain. It does not exclude cross-link cancellation, another tangent mechanism, a nonlocal or coefficient-sensitive signed theorem, or K26, which remains open.
